:module.synapse_workspaces writes secrets (SQL admin username/password, workspace name, RG name) into the keyvault passed via keyvault_id, but has no dependency on :module.keyvault_access_policies. The keyvault access policies that grant the deploying identity permission to create secrets are applied by module.keyvault_access_policies; without ordering, azurerm_key_vault_secret resources in the synapse module can be created before the policies exist and fail with an authorization error. Every other secret-writing consumer (mssql_servers, virtual_machines, azuread_applications, azuread_users) already declares depends_on = [module.keyvault_access_policies] — synapse_workspaces is missing it.

:resource.azurerm_virtual_hub_connection.vhub_connection already depends on :module.virtual_wans implicitly because its virtual_hub_id argument references module.virtual_wans[...].virtual_hubs[...].id (captured as implicit dep on module.virtual_wans:output.virtual_hubs). The explicit depends_on entry for module.virtual_wans duplicates that dependency and can be removed.

module.azuread_applications:resource.null_resource.grant_admin_consent already depends on module.azuread_applications:resource.azuread_service_principal.app implicitly (it reads azuread_service_principal.app.id in its provisioner environment and azuread_application.app), so the explicit depends_on = [azuread_service_principal.app] duplicates an existing dependency.

module.app_service_environments:data.external.ase_ilb_ip already depends on module.app_service_environments:resource.azurerm_template_deployment.ase implicitly (its program interpolates azurerm_template_deployment.ase.outputs into the az CLI command), so the explicit depends_on = [azurerm_template_deployment.ase] duplicates an existing dependency.
